  "what_the_study_did": "The study developed and validated the ZeGlobalTox assay, an innovative experimental procedure using zebrafish larvae to assess organ-specific drug toxicity (cardio-, neuro-, and hepatotoxicity) as a proxy to predict human organ toxicity.",
  "what_it_found": "The ZeGlobalTox assay demonstrated high predictive potential, achieving 89% specificity, 68% sensitivity, and 78% accuracy in predicting human toxicity, reinforcing the utility of zebrafish as a model for early drug safety assessment.",
  "key_quotes": [
    {
      "quote": "We will show that by using ZeGlobaltox, a high toxicity predictivity is achieved—specificity (89%), sensitivity (68%), and accuracy (78%).",
      "topic": "Predictive Performance"
    },
    {
      "quote": "These results reinforce the validation of zebrafish as a suitable model for pre-mammalian studies to reduce and/or replace mammalian vertebrate usage, experimental time, and cost during the process of drug discovery and development.",
      "topic": "Zebrafish Model Validation"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Results obtained through the ZeGlobalTox assay show high sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy values when we compare the zebrafish experimental data with known human toxicity outputs ( Table 3 ).",
      "topic": "Assay Validation"
    },
    {
      "quote": "However, our experimental methodology—drug exposure timing, chosen drug concentration, image acquisition, and image analysis—might require some further improvement to facilitate a more accurate detection of some of the analysed parameters.",
      "topic": "Methodology Limitations"
    },
    {
      "quote": "On the other hand, better sensitivity is indeed required because five compounds known to produce some kind of neurotoxicity in humans did not alter larvae locomotion significantly.",
      "topic": "Neurotoxicity Sensitivity"
    },
    {
      "quote": "In that regard, zebrafish could become the chosen model to bridge the gap between low predictive but high throughput in vitro studies and high predictive but expensive and time-consuming in vivo mammalian studies.",
      "topic": "Bridging Study Gap"
    }
  ]
